subject: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu
content:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Amara Diallo <amara.diallo@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Brian Murphy <brian.murphy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 21, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu

Team,

We need to lock the cross-SDK retry defaults this week so Dana/Mateusz can land implementations early next week and we don’t slip the parity timeline.

Ask: can Platform (Ethan/Amara/Brian) + SRE (Rafael/Tomáš) review the proposal below and reply with either:
- ✅ approve as-is, or
- ✅ approve with specific edits, or
- ❌ block (and why)

Deadline: EOD Thu (1/23). If we don’t hear back, we’ll treat as “approve with no blockers” and proceed, but I’d strongly prefer explicit sign-off.

Proposed default retry policy (hosted API SDKs: Python/TS/Go)

1) Retryable cases
- HTTP 429 (rate limit): retry if Retry-After is present OR with backoff if not present
- HTTP 500/502/503/504
- Transport errors: connect reset, DNS failures, TLS handshake failures, “socket hang up”/EOF before headers
- NOT retryable by default: 4xx other than 429; JSON parse errors; client-side validation errors

2) Budget + attempts
- Max attempts: 3 total (1 initial + up to 2 retries)
- Retry budget: cap total retry time at 20s (across attempts) for non-streaming requests
- Streaming: do not auto-retry mid-stream disconnects by default (separate policy)

3) Backoff
- Exponential backoff with full jitter
- Base: 250ms; Max delay: 4s
- Honor Retry-After when present (with a max cap to avoid extremely long sleeps)

4) Safety + observability
- Surface retry count + final status in error objects
- Emit a lightweight client hook/callback (opt-in) for retry/timeout metrics
- Always propagate and log (redacted) request-id from response headers for support/debugging

Context: SUP-9334 shows TS retrying too aggressively on 429 in a way that extended throttling. We want safe defaults that reduce support load without creating retry storms.

Attachments/links:
- Retry-Standard-v0.9 (Google Doc link)
- ADR-0137 draft (Confluence link)
- API standards: client retry + idempotency guidelines (Confluence link)
- Linear ENG-2482

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Director, Developer Experience (SDKs)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Amara Diallo <amara.diallo@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Brian Murphy <brian.murphy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 21, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu

Adding a couple clarifications from the doc (since I expect these questions):

- For 429: if Retry-After exists, we sleep Retry-After +/- jitter (bounded). If it’s missing, we use standard exponential w/ jitter and still count against budget.
- We will not retry any non-idempotent requests unless we have an Idempotency-Key present (we’ll expose the header; default behavior is “caller decides”). For the hosted endpoints we’re touching right now (chat/completions/embeddings), they’re safe if the caller provides an idempotency key. Otherwise, default is no special-casing.
- The 20s budget is for non-streaming only. For streaming, the default is: if the stream drops after headers / after emitting events, we surface an error + partial content and do not transparently restart.

If Platform can confirm which headers are guaranteed (request-id and retry-after; any standard error code field), it’ll help us get the error taxonomy consistent.

Ibrahim


---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Amara Diallo <amara.diallo@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Brian Murphy <brian.murphy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 21, 2025 at 1:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu

SRE view: generally supportive, but two changes I’d request to reduce amplification risk.

1) 503 handling: Please keep 503 retryable, but make sure we treat 503 + “over capacity” errors similarly to 429 (i.e., follow Retry-After when present). When Retry-After isn’t present, exponential jitter is fine.

2) Budget: 20s total retry budget is OK for non-streaming, but please ensure it’s “wall clock from first attempt start” not “sum of sleeps” so we don’t end up with weird behavior when the first attempt hangs near timeout. (This may be implemented as “overall request deadline” + retries within it.)

Also, we should be explicit in the spec that we don’t retry on timeouts by default unless the timeout is at connect phase (e.g., no bytes read). Retrying on read timeouts caused some nasty spikes in another service.

Tomáš and I can help with suggested wording for the conformance tests (429 burst, 503 flap, and a “slow read timeout” case).

- Rafael


---

From: Amara Diallo <amara.diallo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Brian Murphy <brian.murphy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 22, 2025 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu

On guaranteed headers/payload:

- Response header: request-id is always present on gateway responses (success + error). It’s currently “request-id” (not x-request-id).
- Retry-After: present on 429 and on some 503 paths (capacity protection). Not guaranteed for every 503 today, but we’re improving coverage.
- Rate limit payload: 429 JSON includes a stable error “code” field. PR in progress to standardize fields (code, message, param, type) and include a machine-readable “retry_after_ms” as well.

On idempotency:
- For chat/completions: server does not currently enforce idempotency keys, but we’re aligned that SDK should not assume safe retry for potentially non-idempotent semantics. I agree with Ibrahim’s wording: expose Idempotency-Key, but don’t auto-generate it.

One more note: we’ve seen customers blindly retrying and also retrying in parallel. Please ensure the SDKs serialize retries per request and don’t introduce concurrency.

Amara
API Gateway Engineering


---

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Amara Diallo <amara.diallo@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Brian Murphy <brian.murphy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 23, 2025 at 11:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu

✅ Platform approve with edits (non-blocking) — thanks for pushing this.

Edits requested:
1) Align wording with gateway guarantees:
- request-id header is “request-id” (as Amara said). Please reflect in SDK docs and ensure we log it in a consistent field name.

2) Retry-After handling:
- Add explicit cap (e.g., max 10s) even if Retry-After is higher; beyond that we’d rather fail fast and let callers decide. (This avoids surprising delays in client apps.)

3) Timeout/retry interaction (agree with SRE):
- Don’t retry read timeouts by default. Retrying connect timeouts / handshake errors is OK.

Timeline: If you can incorporate the above into ADR-0137 today, we’ll consider sign-off complete. Amara can take a pass on the final language by EOD.

Ethan
Engineering Manager, Platform Control Plane


---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Amara Diallo <amara.diallo@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Brian Murphy <brian.murphy@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 23, 2025 at 4:28 PM PT
Subject: Re: Retry defaults proposal (SDK parity): request for Platform + SRE sign-off by Thu

Thanks all — incorporating edits now. Summary of what we’ll lock for v1:

- Retryable: 429, 500/502/503/504, transport/connect/handshake errors, EOF-before-headers
- Not retryable: other 4xx, parse/validation errors, read timeouts
- Attempts: 3 total (1 + 2)
- Budget: non-streaming overall “retry window” bounded to 20s wall-clock from first attempt start
- Backoff: exp + full jitter; base 250ms; max 4s
- Retry-After: honored when present, capped at 10s (still jittered)
- request-id: read from response header “request-id”; surfaced in error objects and safe logs
- No mid-stream auto-retry by default (handled under streaming ADR)

Next steps:
- Ibrahim will update ADR-0137 + the SDK spec doc tonight and tag Amara for a final read.
- Once Amara gives a 👍, I’ll mark Platform+SRE sign-off in ENG-2482 and unblock SDK PRs.
- Rafael/Tomáš: we’ll follow up tomorrow to align on the exact conformance tests for “slow read timeout” + 503 flap.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Monica
